questions.stem: Jahangir (r. 1605-1627) succeeded Akbar. His chief queen, who wielded enormous influence and was the power behind the throne, was:
questions.explanation: NUR JAHAN (born Mehr-un-Nissa in 1577; married Jahangir in 1611 as his 20th wife) was the ONLY Mughal empress to have coins struck in her name, issue farmans, and effectively co-rule. Formed a 'JUNTA' with her father ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH (Prime Minister), brother ASAF KHAN, and step-son SHAH JAHAN. Her niece ARJUMAND BANU (later MUMTAZ MAHAL) was Shah Jahan's wife — for whom the Taj Mahal was built. Jahangir (Salim) also wrote the 'TUZUK-I-JAHANGIRI' memoir. He was an art patron (Mughal miniature painting peak — Ustad Mansur, Abul Hasan). British East India Company's William Hawkins (1608) and Thomas Roe (1616) visited his court. Tomb: Shahdara Bagh, Lahore.

questions.stem: Shah Jahan built the TAJ MAHAL as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. In which years was construction carried out, and who was the CHIEF ARCHITECT?
questions.explanation: TAJ MAHAL — commissioned 1632 by SHAH JAHAN (r. 1628-58) for his beloved wife MUMTAZ MAHAL who died during childbirth of their 14th child (1631, Burhanpur). Construction: ~22 years, completed 1653. Chief architect: USTAD AHMAD LAHAURI (some sources credit Mirak Mirza Ghiyath, but Lahauri is more accepted). White Makrana marble. 42-acre complex with char-bagh, mosque (West), jawab (East — mirror-image of mosque but unconsecrated, just for symmetry), gateway, minarets (tilt outward so earthquake doesn't damage the main tomb). UNESCO WHS 1983. Both Shah Jahan and Mumtaz are interred here. Shah Jahan's OTHER architecture: RED FORT DELHI (1648 — with Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas), JAMA MASJID DELHI (1656), MOTI MASJID (Agra), PEACOCK THRONE (Takht-i-Taus).

questions.stem: The War of Succession among Shah Jahan's sons was won by Aurangzeb, who executed his brother Dara Shikoh (the liberal scholar-prince). Dara Shikoh is best known for translating which Hindu texts into Persian?
questions.explanation: DARA SHIKOH (1615-1659), Shah Jahan's eldest son and heir apparent, was a Sufi-leaning scholar who sought syncretism between Islam and Hinduism. His magnum opus: 'SIRR-I-AKBAR' (The Great Secret, 1657) — Persian translation of 52 Upanishads. He also wrote 'MAJMA-UL-BAHRAIN' ('Mingling of Two Oceans') arguing that Islamic Sufism and Hindu Vedanta teach the same truth. This earned him charges of apostasy. The WAR OF SUCCESSION (1657-59): Aurangzeb defeated Dara at the BATTLE OF SAMUGARH (May 1658) near Agra. Dara was captured, paraded in humiliation through Delhi, tried for apostasy, and BEHEADED (1659). His body buried anonymously at Humayun's tomb. Shah Jahan was imprisoned in Agra Fort by Aurangzeb till his death 1666 (buried next to Mumtaz in Taj).

questions.stem: Aurangzeb (r. 1658-1707) reversed several liberal policies of his predecessors. He re-imposed which tax in 1679 that had been abolished by Akbar in 1564?
questions.explanation: JIZYA — a poll tax on non-Muslim subjects in exchange for protection (dhimmi status) — was abolished by AKBAR in 1564 as part of his Sulh-i-Kul (peace with all) policy. AURANGZEB re-imposed it on 2 April 1679 — a major departure from Mughal syncretism, alienating Rajput and Hindu subjects, contributing to Maratha and Jat uprisings. Jizya was finally abolished by Farrukhsiyar in 1712 (briefly re-imposed, then abolished by Muhammad Shah 1719 permanently). Aurangzeb's other 'orthodox' measures: banned music at court, imposed Sharia law rigorously, demolished several temples (Kashi Vishwanath 1669, Keshava Rai Mathura, Somnath), ordered FATAWA-I-ALAMGIRI compilation (Hanafi fiqh digest). Title: ALAMGIR ('Conqueror of the World').

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's Deccan campaigns (1681-1707) — fighting the Marathas and Deccan Sultanates — lasted 26 years. Which two Deccan Sultanates did he annex?

options.option_text: Ahmednagar (1636 — during Shah Jahan) and Berar

questions.explanation: The five Deccan Sultanates (15th-17th c. successors of the Bahmani): AHMEDNAGAR (conquered by Shah Jahan 1636), BIJAPUR (Adil Shahi — annexed by Aurangzeb 1686), GOLCONDA (Qutb Shahi — annexed by Aurangzeb 1687), BIDAR (absorbed by Bijapur 1619), BERAR (absorbed by Ahmednagar). Thus Aurangzeb completed Mughal unification of the Deccan. But simultaneously, he was fighting MARATHAS under SHIVAJI (d. 1680) and his son SAMBHAJI (captured and executed 1689). Despite imprisoning Shivaji at Agra in 1666 (Shivaji escaped in a basket), he could never break the Marathas. His Deccan stay 1681-1707 drained Mughal resources + alienated nobility. Aurangzeb died at Aurangabad (1707) — buried simply at Khuldabad (Rauza). Empire began crumbling within a decade.

questions.stem: The famous PEACOCK THRONE (Takht-i-Taus) of Shah Jahan — studded with the KOH-I-NOOR diamond — was looted in 1739 by:
questions.explanation: NADIR SHAH of Persia (1688-1747) invaded India in 1739, defeated Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah at the BATTLE OF KARNAL (Feb 1739), and sacked DELHI — massacred ~30,000, looted the Peacock Throne, Koh-i-Noor diamond, Jam-e-Jam, and treasure estimated at 70 crore rupees. He took it all to Persia. Peacock Throne's gold: disassembled, ultimately lost. KOH-I-NOOR travelled: Nadir (1739) → after his assassination, to Ahmad Shah Durrani → Afghan king Shah Shuja (1813) → gifted under duress to Maharaja RANJIT SINGH of Punjab → after Anglo-Sikh Wars, BRITISH East India Company (Lord Dalhousie, 1849) → Queen Victoria (1850) → currently in Crown Jewels, Tower of London. India has demanded repatriation. AHMAD SHAH ABDALI/DURRANI invaded India 8 times between 1748-1767 (famous: 3rd Panipat 1761 — defeated Marathas).

questions.stem: The last Mughal emperor was Bahadur Shah II 'Zafar' — a poet and symbolic leader. After the 1857 Revolt, what happened to him?

options.option_text: Executed by the British in Delhi
Tried for treason, exiled to Rangoon, Burma, where he died in 1862
Restored to symbolic throne under British control

questions.explanation: BAHADUR SHAH II 'Zafar' (1775-1862) — the 20th and last Mughal Emperor — was proclaimed 'Emperor of Hindustan' by the 1857 rebel sepoys in Delhi. After the British recapture of Delhi (Sept 1857), he was TRIED for treason (Jan 1858), convicted, and EXILED to Rangoon, Burma (1858), where he died in 1862 aged 87. His wife Zeenat Mahal and remaining family went with him. His sons MIRZA MUGHAL, KHIZR SULTAN, MIRZA ABU BAKR were shot dead by MAJOR WILLIAM HODSON near Khooni Darwaza (Bloody Gate), Delhi — ending the imperial line. Zafar was a prolific Urdu poet ('Na kisi ki aankh ka noor hoon...' famously attributed but actually by Muztar Khairabadi). Tomb: Yangon, Myanmar. The 1857 defeat effectively ENDED Mughal rule (though nominal since 1803) and transferred India to direct British Crown rule via the Government of India Act 1858.

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's conflict with the Sikh Gurus led to the execution of which Guru, subsequently called 'Hind di Chadar' (Shield of India)?
questions.explanation: GURU TEGH BAHADUR (9th Sikh Guru, 1621-1675) was executed on 24 November 1675 in Chandni Chowk, Delhi, by order of AURANGZEB. His refusal to convert to Islam AND his defence of Kashmiri Pandits (who came to him for protection against forced conversion) led to his martyrdom. Title: HIND DI CHADAR ('Shield of India'). His son Gobind Rai became the 10th Guru GURU GOBIND SINGH (1666-1708), who later founded the KHALSA at Anandpur on BAISAKHI 1699. Guru Gobind Singh's four sons (sahibzadas) were all martyred: two (elder) killed in battle at Chamkaur (1704); two (younger — Zorawar Singh 9 and Fateh Singh 6) bricked alive in walls at Sirhind on refusal to convert (Dec 1705). Guru Gobind Singh declared the GURU GRANTH SAHIB as the eternal Guru (1708). Earlier: GURU ARJAN DEV (5th) was executed by JAHANGIR in 1606 — first Sikh martyr.

questions.stem: Jahangir's tomb is at Lahore. Whose tomb is located at Sikandra (near Agra)?
questions.explanation: Mughal tomb locations (important for SSC/UPSC): BABUR — ARAM BAGH, Kabul, Afghanistan (as per his wish, initially interred at Agra then moved). HUMAYUN — HUMAYUN'S TOMB, Delhi (1565-72, UNESCO WHS). AKBAR — SIKANDRA, Agra (completed by Jahangir 1613). JAHANGIR — SHAHDARA BAGH, Lahore (Pakistan). SHAH JAHAN — inside the TAJ MAHAL, Agra, next to his wife Mumtaz. AURANGZEB — KHULDABAD (near Aurangabad), Maharashtra — a simple unmarked tomb per his wish (in contrast to his ancestors' grand mausoleums). BAHADUR SHAH II ZAFAR — YANGON, Myanmar. NUR JAHAN and ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH — separate tombs in Lahore and Agra respectively. ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH'S TOMB (1622-28) at Agra is nicknamed 'Baby Taj' — early example of pietra dura, precursor to the Taj Mahal.

questions.stem: SHAH JAHAN built which of the following as his symbol of sovereignty upon shifting his capital from Agra to Delhi in 1648?

options.option_text: Red Fort (Lal Qila) + city of Shahjahanabad

questions.explanation: SHAH JAHAN shifted the Mughal capital from AGRA to DELHI in 1648. He built RED FORT (LAL QILA) — 1638-1648 — and around it, the new capital SHAHJAHANABAD (today's OLD DELHI: Chandni Chowk, Jama Masjid, etc.). Red Fort features: DIWAN-I-AM (Hall of Public Audience, with the famous PIETRA DURA ARCH with original PEACOCK THRONE), DIWAN-I-KHAS (Hall of Private Audience), RANG MAHAL, MOTI MASJID (Pearl Mosque), HAYAT-BAKSH BAGH. UNESCO WHS since 2007. Today, the INDIAN PRIME MINISTER hoists the TRICOLOUR from the LAHORI GATE of the Red Fort every 15 AUGUST. JAMA MASJID (also Shah Jahan, 1656) is India's largest mosque. Qutb Minar was built by Qutbuddin Aibak (1193-1220s) + Iltutmish; Humayun's Tomb by Hamida Banu Begum (1565-72); Purana Qila by Sher Shah + Humayun.
